_comment: The CI tooling runs inside xmake's Lua sandbox, which is neither plain
Lua nor LuaJIT: it ADDS globals (import, try/catch, raise, cprint, path,
hash, and the task DSL) and REMOVES several standard ones. Without this
file the language server flags every one of those additions as an
undefined global, which buries real findings under noise.
It also records what the sandbox takes AWAY. Each of the removed globals
below cost a debugging round trip when it turned out to be missing at
run time rather than at edit time.
'lowercase-global' is disabled because xmake's module system REQUIRES
it: a module exports by assigning global functions, and 'local function'
would make them invisible to import(). It is a correct diagnostic for
ordinary Lua and a structurally wrong one here.
workspace.library points at ci/meta, which declares the xmake APIs this
project calls. Those declarations bring completion and type checking;
disabling 'undefined-field' instead would have silenced 140 findings and
every real one along with them.
